title: POC Weekly Sync - Dedicated Sizing & Autoscale Planning
summary: Weekly POC sync to review pilot results and iterate on Dedicated sizing and autoscaling policies. Discussed p99 latency spikes during traffic bursts, current Dedicated pool utilization, burst capacity options, fallback model variants, KV/prefix cache impact, and security requirements (VPC & KMS). Agreed next steps: Redwood to share pricing and burst policy, schedule stress test, and provide tuned autoscale proposal.

transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-04-13
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Ethan Cole (Redwood CSM); Mike Donovan, Sara Kim, Ravi Patel, Lena Torres (VectorHealth)

Auto-generated Summary: Weekly POC follow-up; focus on Dedicated sizing & autoscale.

[00:00] Jordan: Alright folks, thanks for joining. Quick roll call, then we'll jump into the numbers from last week's run.
[00:16] Mike: Hi everyone, Mike here. We had couple infra people on earlier but they're on this call now.
[00:23] Priya: Hey. Thanks. So I pulled the telemetry from the Dedicated pool, and overall throughput looks good, steady state about 120 inferred tokens per second -- sorry 120 requests per minute at our default batch sizing? (laughs) -- so some of the labels in the dashboard are off, but you get the picture.
[00:40] Sara: Yeah, the steady baseline is fine. Our problem is the bursts, we saw p95/p99 jump a lot when marketing campaign started sending traffic. p99 hit like 2.3 seconds which is outside our SLO.
[00:56] Priya: Right, and that correlates with queueing in the request router. We configured min nodes=2, max=8 for the Dedicated pool, autoscaler target CPU util 70% with a 60s scale cooldown. The issue is network + KV cache warmup during cold scale events.
[01:14] Jordan: To clarify, when you say KV cache warmup can you describe the pattern? Is it prefix cache misses causing longer first-token latencies?
[01:23] Priya: Exactly. The prefix / KV cache isn't fully warmed on newly provisioned instances so early requests hit the slower path. We also saw some tokenization overhead with big prompts.
[01:33] Mike: Is there a way to reserve burst capacity? We don't want to overprovision 24/7 but need headroom for these marketing spikes.
[01:41] Jordan: Yes, we have two levers: 1) dedicated burst instances — you can reserve a small pool that stays warm, 2) fast-burst policy that temporarily allows oversubscribe into a larger capacity tier for short windows, or 3) fallback to a lighter-weight model variant (quantized) for bursts. Each has tradeoffs.
[01:59] Ravi: What's the cost delta for keeping, say, 2 warm nodes vs relying on autoscale with faster cooldown?
[02:06] Priya: Rough numbers: keeping 2 warm nodes is predictable but costs about X% extra monthly; fast-burst policy is cheaper but requires we keep a warm cache mechanism to avoid the initial latency hit. Fallback model reduces cost and latency but may reduce quality slightly. I'll put concrete numbers in the autoscale config doc.
[02:24] Sara: Also we need to consider KMS key startup -- onboarding their HSM and key service caused a ~200ms handshake on new instances last week. That contributed to the p99.
[02:36] Jordan: Thanks — good callout. We'll note that in the SRE runbook.
[02:41] (Short crosstalk)
[02:48] Priya: For the tuned autoscale proposal I recommend: min nodes=2, target util 65%, max nodes=10, cooldown 45s, and keep one warm 'burst' node pinned for 24/7 that handles prefix cache priming. Also add a policy: for traffic above 160 RPS auto-failover to quantized variant with same interface.
[03:12] Mike: Does the failover require code changes? Our dev team wants minimal integration effort.
[03:19] Priya: No, the routing is transparent. We can route by policy at the request layer — the API remains the same. We will add a header you can observe during the rollout but it's not required for your app to change.
[03:32] Ravi: Ok good. On security we still need the Private / VPC flow and KMS integration, plus audit logs for token-level tracing. Are those incremental to Dedicated or part of Private?
[03:43] Jordan: Dedicated supports VPC peering and customer KMS. Audit logs can be shipped to your SIEM — we'll share the doc. For fully air-gapped on-prem that would be Redwood Private, but from what we've seen Dedicated + VPC meets most enterprise needs.
[03:56] Lena: One more thing — we noticed a KV cache key mismatch because of a slight prompt whitespace difference; that caused cache misses. Can Redwood help with prefix normalization suggestions?
[04:06] Priya: We can share recommended deterministic normalization (trim, collapse whitespace, hash prefixes). Also suggest using a small client-side prefix cache for high-frequency tokens.
[04:16] Jordan: Let's talk about the proposed stress test. We suggested a 3 hour sustained 200 RPS run with three bursts of 5 minutes at 350 RPS to capture the worst-case scale behavior. That should surface cold start latency and any KMS handshake issues.
[04:31] Mike: We can run that. We'll schedule it over a low-traffic window and share logs.
[04:36] Priya: Great. After we get the logs we'll tune autoscale thresholds and give you a model for expected cost per 1M tokens under that traffic pattern.
[04:46] Jordan: Competitor question — Mike, you mentioned your infra team looked at a couple other options last month. Anything we should be worried about in the decision process (OpenAI or SageMaker)?
[04:57] Mike: OpenAI is simpler to integrate but cost was higher for our volumes; SageMaker gives control but ops overhead is heavy. You're competing on predictable latency and cost which is why this POC matters.
[05:09] Ethan: Quick note: I'll upload the Dedicated sizing deck and the benchmark spreadsheet (link pasted in chat).
[05:16] Jordan: Perfect. Let's do a quick recap of action items and owners...
[05:22] (recap)
[05:24] Jordan: Jordan to send pricing + example burst-policy. Priya to send autoscale config. VectorHealth to run stress test and share logs. Mike to confirm success criteria. We'll reconvene after the stress test and tuning for a deep-dive the week of April 20th.
[05:40] Mike: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
